chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Moving to Chicago, marrying Louella Brown and the One-Nighters Joe circuit
summary: He settled in Chicago with Louella and toured the South every summer doing one-nighters beside Ray Charles and B. B. King.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We run into a lot of people down there used to book dances. So's we worked for them all through Texas. I was down in Texas so much until I lived down there. So when I leave Texas, I'd go home. I lived in Chicago. I moved up in Chicago where I met a lady. Her name was Louella Brown. I wrote a song about her--Louella Brown. So I met her in Chicago, and I...we got married. I lived with her seventeen years. She used to travel on the road with me, and we had a ball. We bought several homes in Chicago. I had coupla flats in Chicago, and we were makin' it good.

Then, every summer we take off and go down through Texas and Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee. We play all over the South. I don't think there's a place in the South where I ain't never been. I made so many stops...one-nighters...call me "One-Nighters Joe." 'Course, Ray Charles, Bobby Blue Bland, B.B. King an' all them fellows, they were doin' the same thing. That's all we played was one-nighters. We didn't play too many nightclubs. When we did, we just stayed three days... weekends...and we had a lot of fun together. We used to all meet up together in this restaurant and have a ball. They sold bootleg whiskey there. 'Course you could go to the liquor store and get whiskey but this place didn't have no whiskey license but they bootlegged.
